Karnak Temple

Luxor, East Bank · You're looking at the Great Hypostyle Hall

Hours6:00 AMIn 20 min
Ticket600 EGPStudent 300
CrowdLowPeaks 9–11 AM

The story

For 2,000 years, every pharaoh wanted his name on Karnak. What began as a modest shrine to Amun-Re around 1970 BC grew into the largest religious complex ever built. The hall around you was raised by Seti I and finished by his son Ramesses II — a forest of 134 stone papyrus stalks, once painted blue, red and gold.

Great Hypostyle Hall, KarnakFrom your snap · 5:41 AM
Today 5:42 AM
Who built this hall? It's enormous.
It was started by Seti I around 1290 BC and finished by his son Ramesses II. Look straight up: the 12 central columns are about 21 m tall with open papyrus capitals, and you can still see traces of the original blue and red paint near the top.
Wander AtlasKarnak Hypostyle Hall Project
Is the Sacred Lake worth it, or should I skip it?
Go now. It's a 4-minute walk south-east, and the tour groups will fill the hall from about 9 AM. Next to the lake is the giant granite scarab of Amenhotep III — locals walk around it seven times for good luck.
